question.text: Nalanda VC Fund's loss-making investee Mithila SaaS has FY24 revenue of INR 80 crore (no profit). Listed SaaS peers trade at EV/Revenue of 8x. Applying 35% DLOM, what is the estimated EV?

explanation.text: The Logic: Unlisted EV/Revenue multiple = 8 x (1 - 0.35) = 5.2x. EV = 5.2 x 80 = INR 416 crore. For loss-making SaaS, EV/Revenue is the IPEV-endorsed default because EV/EBITDA and P/E are undefined. The Trap: INR 640 ignores DLOM; INR 400 uses 5x (wrong math); INR 520 uses 20% DLOM. Early-stage SaaS typically warrants 30-40% DLOM given illiquidity and execution risk. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical revenue-multiple logic. XXI-B rarely uses it because most listed PMS stocks are profitable. XV uses PSR (Price/Sales) instead of EV/Revenue — the difference is debt inclusion. Manager's Pro-Tip: For pre-revenue deep-tech in Cat I VC, even EV/Revenue is useless — fall back to precedent-transaction 'pre-money per engineer' or 'per patent' heuristics, and disclose the primitive multiple in your PPM.
